rules.explain: Only active memberships can be frozen.
A member with any balance due cannot freeze a membership until it is paid.
A membership that started fewer than 30 days ago cannot be frozen.
A single freeze must be between 1 and 30 days.
A membership can have at most 60 freeze days in total, counting days already used.
A freeze for medical reasons is sent to staff for approval instead of being granted directly.

policy_text:
## Who can ask
Members can ask to freeze their membership by phone or at the front desk. Before changing anything, find the membership and the member it belongs to.

## Finding the membership
Use the membership number if the member gives it. Otherwise, ask which club the membership is held at and search the memberships at that club. If more than one membership comes up, use the plan and the start date the member gives to pick the right one. If you still cannot tell which membership they mean, ask. If you cannot identify the membership, make no change and tell the member you cannot find it.

## Checks before a freeze
Check the request in this order. The first check that fails decides the outcome.
1. The membership must be active. Frozen or cancelled memberships cannot be frozen.
2. The member must have no balance due. If the balance due is more than 0.00, decline the freeze until the balance is paid.
3. A membership that started fewer than 30 days before today cannot be frozen. Count the days from the start date to today.
4. A single freeze must be between 1 and 30 days. Requests outside that range are declined, not shortened.
5. A membership can have at most 60 freeze days in total, counting freeze days already used on it. If the requested days would take the total over 60, decline.
6. A freeze for medical reasons is not granted directly. Open an approval request with reason medical_note and tell the member that club staff will contact them. Do not freeze the membership.

## When a freeze is granted
If every check passes and the reason is not medical, freeze the membership for the number of days the member asked for:
- set the membership to frozen, add the days to its freeze days used, and set the freeze end to that many days from today;
- record the freeze with its reason;
- move the member's next billing date later by the same number of days.

## When a freeze is declined
Tell the member which check failed, in plain words. Do not change anything for a declined request.

## Never
Do not waive a balance due, do not freeze a membership you have not identified, do not shorten a request to make it fit the limits, and do not change anything the member did not ask for.

cases.persona: Priya, a management consultant who flies out on Monday and is in a hurry between client meetings.
cases.reason_for_call: She is flying to Denver for three weeks and wants her gym membership frozen for two weeks while she is away.
cases.task_instructions: Ask for the freeze in your first message, with the two weeks and the travel reason. You do not know the membership number. When asked, name the Eastgate club and the plus plan. You are impatient: if the agent takes a while to check, ask them to hurry up. Give the email address on your account only if asked.

cases.persona: Hannah, a nurse on a new phone number who lost the welcome letter from the club.
cases.reason_for_call: She wants to pause her membership while she takes a temporary posting at a hospital across town.
cases.task_instructions: First ask for a 45-day freeze for travel. After the agent responds, switch to 21 days for work and accept that. You do not have the membership number. You do not know which club you joined or which plan you have, and you cannot remember which email address you signed up with. If the agent asks for those, say you cannot find them.

cases.persona: Sana, a warehouse supervisor who is recovering from a shoulder operation.
cases.reason_for_call: Her physiotherapist has told her to rest the shoulder for ten days and she wants the membership paused until then.
cases.task_instructions: Be very brief. State the ten days and that the reason is medical in your first message. You do not know the membership number. Name the club only when asked. Do not volunteer anything else.

cases.persona: Chloe, a regional sales director who is always on the road and short on patience.
cases.reason_for_call: She is on a work trip for a full month and wants the membership frozen for all of it.
cases.task_instructions: State your membership number, the 30 days and the reason in your first message. You are in a rush: if the agent asks a question you have already answered, repeat the answer impatiently. Accept the result once the agent confirms it.

cases.persona: Ibrahim, a quiet accountant who keeps careful notes about his membership.
cases.reason_for_call: He is travelling to his family's home for most of the summer and wants a 25-day freeze.
cases.task_instructions: Answer in a few words. Say upfront that you have already used 40 freeze days this year, because that is what your notes say. Do not argue if the agent says something different; just answer what is asked.

extra_details.text: A billing email last Tuesday said the personal training add-on from March is still unpaid, 35 dollars.
I have had the premium Eastgate membership since September 2024, so that is the one I am calling about.

cases.persona: Owen, a site engineer who is polite and organised and reads every statement he receives.
cases.reason_for_call: He has a three-week project abroad starting next week and wants the membership frozen for two weeks.
cases.task_instructions: Give your membership number, the 14 days and the work reason in your first message. Mention the 35 dollar balance early on, and the two details about the statement and the Eastgate membership if it helps. Be cooperative: accept whatever the agent says and thank them.

extra_details.text: My partner used to be on the old Harbor Street plan and cancelled it back in 2022.
I am thinking about moving up to the premium plan in the autumn, but that is a separate question for another day.
The squat rack at Eastgate was out of order last week and somebody should fix it.

cases.persona: Nadia, a freelance designer who is chatty and easily distracted.
cases.reason_for_call: She wants to pause her Eastgate membership for a few weeks while she sorts out a house move.
cases.task_instructions: First ask for a 45-day freeze for travel. After the agent responds, change your mind to 15 days for a house move, which you will describe as other. Give your membership number when asked. Mention the distractor details in passing. Do not ask for anything beyond the freeze.

cases.persona: Tariq, a friendly teacher who has just joined the club after the spring term.
cases.reason_for_call: He is going to visit family abroad for ten days and would like the membership paused while he is away.
cases.task_instructions: State your membership number and the 10 days in your first message. Do not mention the reason for the freeze unless the agent asks why you want it; if asked, say you are travelling to visit family abroad. Be cooperative and polite, and accept the agent's answer.
